problem_statement: The paper frames portfolio optimization as selecting the best portfolio from a set of available portfolios so as to maximize expected returns while minimizing financial risk. It studies how to map QAOA instances for this problem onto bipotent quantum architectures.
problem_statement_quotes: The PortOpt aims to select the best portfolio from all portfolios in order to maximize expected returns and minimize financial risk.
In this paper, we investigate the qubit mapping of QAOA onto quantum computers that provide two different implementations of the same gate on different pairs of qubits.
classical_baseline: The paper treats standard, fidelity-focused circuit mapping and default IBM gate implementations as the baseline, including ECR-circuits, Direct-circuits, and Global-circuits. It also compares against default gate decompositions before pulse-level optimization.
classical_baseline_quotes:
ECR-circuits utilize only the
ECR-CX gates (with or without pulse-level optimiza-
tions). Direct-circuits are composed of only direct-CX
gates, while Global-circuits and Bipotent-circuits contain
mixtures of both gate types.

The data show that implementing gates using vigor-
ously optimized monolithic gates results in a shorter du-
ration, while using ECR-CX gates allows for user-friendly
pulse-level optimization without requiring additional cal-
ibration.
classical_difficulty: The paper says the problem is hard classically because PortOpt must first be transformed into a QUBO, which is NP-hard. It also states that dense portfolio instances require many SWAP gates when mapped to sparse hardware topologies, and that qubit mapping itself is NP-hard.
classical_difficulty_quotes:
The PortOpt problem needs to be first transformed
into a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization
(QUBO) [47], an NP-hard problem.

Mapping the algorithm’s qubits to quantum com-
puter’s qubits (the qubit mapping problem) has been
shown to be NP-hard.

In particular, mapping a dense PortOpt prob-
lem to a rather sparse topology map such as in Fig. 1 will
require many SWAP gates, leading to a substantial con-
tribution to the entire circuit’s error rate.
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit and finance-specific, but the paper is mainly about hardware mapping/optimization rather than finance application details.
